description: I am a 4th-year in Computer Science at Carleton University. My interests are in software design and Artificial Intelligence. My goals for this hackathon are to broaden my real-world experience with Software development.
summary: Jezero Crater - Mission Planner is a mission-planning application designed to support exploration of a selected 10 km × 10 km area within Jezero Crater on Mars. We selected this region because it contains geologically diverse igneous formations, particularly Máaz and Séítah, providing an opportunity to investigate Mars' ancient volcanic and magmatic history. By studying rocks with different compositions and formation processes, our mission aims to better understand how magma cooled, crystallized, and contributed to shaping the Martian crust. The project focuses on supporting exploration of this scientifically significant region, where geological diversity offers valuable opportunities for investigation. Our goal is to help make the exploration of Mars more informed, efficient, and scientifically valuable.
details:
Jezero Crater - Mission Planner is an interactive mapping and mission-planning application that allows users to explore a selected region of Jezero Crater and plan potential exploration routes. It integrates multiple map layers, including elevation, optical imagery, geological formations, and terrain traversability. Users can switch between these layers, place waypoints at locations of interest, view information about the surrounding terrain, and establish an astronaut starting position. The application also implements the A* pathfinding algorithm to calculate routes between locations while accounting for terrain difficulty and avoiding impassable areas.

A key benefit of the application is that it brings different types of geographical and scientific information together in one interface. This helps users identify promising locations for investigation while considering the practical challenges of navigating the Martian surface. Our intended impact is to demonstrate how combining geological data with terrain-aware route planning can make planetary exploration safer, more efficient, and more scientifically productive.

We developed the application primarily using Python, with PyQGIS and QGIS for geographic visualization and map interaction. GDAL and NumPy were used for raster data processing and terrain analysis, while we implemented our own A* pathfinding algorithm for route planning.

Our creative approach was to combine geological exploration and navigation into a single mission-planning tool. During development, we considered the scientific value of the selected region, the availability and alignment of map datasets, terrain difficulty, impassable areas, and the usability of the interface. These considerations helped us create an application that balances scientific exploration with practical navigation needs.
